exposure: Number of vacuum pop-offs during delivery
cohort: 1730 women with singleton pregnancies who delivered via vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery (VAVD) or a trial of VAVD followed by cesarean delivery
finding: Having any number of vacuum pop-offs during delivery was associated with an increase in adverse neonatal outcomes, including scalp/facial lacerations, intracranial hemorrhage, convulsions, CNS depression, and NICU admission.
